title: Choose CalenderJS's visual world
question: The roll assigned Swiss Transit Timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Swiss Transit Timetable
options.lineage: SBB station clock + DIN transit wayfinding + printed departure timetables
options.thesis: CalenderJS as the station clock: one red second-hand sweep, grid-precise time, zero ambiguity about what happens when.
options.viewport: A full-bleed timetable grid: the hero IS a live departures board where rows are real DSL-validated event types, the red second-hand sweeps across a header rule, one primary action (Run the demo) sits where a platform number would.
options.risk: Reads as 'generic transit dashboard' if the grid loosens or the red accent spreads past one committed sweep.

raised.raise: The validation/DSL section renders as a canvas-drawn black/white data field (seeded, reduced-motion safe) proving rules at work, not a static diagram.

options.label: Punch Card Ledger
options.lineage: Hollerith punch cards + mechanical tabulator printouts
options.thesis: Every event type is a punched row: holes are the DSL rules, and an invalid edit simply will not punch.
options.viewport: The hero is one oversized punch card; each column a DSL field, cutouts showing which fields are editable/validated for the current event type.
options.risk: Also the direction most 'dev tool meets retro computing' sites land on — familiar nostalgia rather than a fresh read.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda datamatics: barcode columns, sine lattices, pure black/white
options.thesis: The DSL's validation rules rendered as a strobing black-and-white data field, columns snapping to valid/invalid.
options.case: Fuses cleanly onto the validation-engine story (rigor, precision, zero-grey certainty); loses narrowly on domain fit — pure data abstraction reads less like 'a calendar' than the timetable does.
options.risk: Can read as generic 'data art' decoration if the bars do not actually visualize real validation states.
options.kept: Donated its black/white/canvas-rendered discipline to the assigned direction's DSL demo section.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.lineage: film editing bench: perforated select rail, pinned frames, tape flags
options.thesis: Events strung on a perforated timeline rail, state shown as a mark (grease cross, tape flag, pin) rather than a colour.
options.case: Fuses on state-as-mark, but film editing is not this audience's world — loses on audience identification against developers evaluating a scheduling library.
options.kept: Its state-as-mark discipline (a flag, a cross, a pin — never a colour swap) for how the assigned direction should render permission-denied vs validated rows.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dev-tool landing page every library ships: dark hero, gradient headline, code snippet on the right, feature cards below.
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline and subcopy over a dark ground, code sample floating right, three-up feature cards below the fold.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dev-tool homepage by design.
